verdict.why: Both avideo_extension and avideo_status run the same async-wrapper sequence. They set kwargs['async_call']=True and build a partial of the sync function. They copy the contextvars context and run it in the default executor. If the result is a coroutine they await it. On any Exception they re-raise via litellm.exception_type with model='', the provider, and local_vars/kwargs. Only the target sync function and its specific arguments (prompt and seconds versus none) differ. This sequence is already repeated across the video module's async wrappers, so a shared helper makes sense, e.g. `_run_sync_in_executor_with_async_call(func, provider, local_vars, **kwargs)`. Each public function would keep its own signature, docstring and argument list. This is a partial overlap: the wrapper and error-mapping boilerplate, not the endpoint-specific parameters.
